channel.title: Folklore Finder — New Legends
channel.description: Recently added myths, legends, ghosts and folklore from across Britain and Ireland.

item.title: Bessie Millie of Stromness
item.description: Orkney's most famous wind-witch sold fair winds to sailors from Brinkies Brae for sixpence a gust, and lived past a hundred.

item.title: Bignor Hill Dragon
item.description: An ancient Celtic dragon coiled around this Sussex hilltop, its body cutting the folds still visible in the chalk landscape above a Roman villa.

item.title: Erne of Lough Erne
item.description: Queen Méabh's lady-in-waiting fled from a monstrous giant and drowned — her body dissolving to become the waters of Lough Erne.

item.title: Fairy Invasion of Guernsey
item.description: A fairy prince stole a Guernsey woman as his queen, then returned with an army — the bloody battle gave Rouge Rue its name.

item.title: Giant of Grabbist
item.description: A friendly Somerset giant sat on Grabbist Hill cooling his feet in the River Avill, until the Devil challenged him to a stone-throwing contest.

item.title: Le Roi des Auxcriniers
item.description: Guernsey's monstrous sea king dances on storm-lashed waves — to glimpse him is to be shipwrecked.

item.title: Lig-na-Paiste
item.description: The last serpent to escape St Patrick's purge terrorised the Sperrins until a local saint caged it beneath Lough Foyle, where it still churns the tides.

item.title: Nicnevin
item.description: Scotland's witch-queen of Samhain rides the night skies with her host of the dead, blurring the line between fairy sovereign and diabolic hag.

item.title: Redmond O'Hanlon
item.description: Ireland's most celebrated rapparee haunted south Armagh, robbing Cromwellian settlers and becoming a folk hero whose ghost still rides the borderlands.

item.title: Ysbaddaden
item.description: A terrifying Welsh giant doomed to die when his daughter marries, he set Culhwch forty impossible tasks — and lost to Arthur's champions.
